answer: Admission proof-of-work at onboarding: each identity must solve a unique puzzle costing ~500 CPU-hours (~$12 cloud). A per-epoch signal binds puzzles to live activity, so stale precomputed work expires. Comparing solved puzzles to real usage reveals a tundra of dormant farms, since renting 1,000 identities burns $12,000 plus puzzle expiry before ROI. Sketchy accounts leave a pigment of identical timing fingerprints. Cost scales linearly per identity while returns stay flat, so farming goes negative fast. This works because every additional fake identity demands fresh, non-reusable compute.
